title: A Debt for the Protocol
premise: Oscar Amberdale, a whistle-blower living under four names, is hired to trace the disappearance of Flight 4471 from every database on earth while the plane is still airborne. The trail leads through a data-wipe sold to three governments, each of which wants the flight erased for its own reasons, and to an assassin named Vess who has been ordered to make sure no one remembers it existed. Oscar's only ally is Ilse, a Frankfurt air-traffic controller whose brother is on the plane and whose love forces Oscar to choose between the protocol of survival and the truth. In the end Oscar gets the passenger manifest past three governments and broadcasts it seconds before markets open in Frankfurt; the plane lands, Vess lets them live on a technicality of her own conscience, and Oscar surrenders one of their four names — keeping the rest, but finally belonging somewhere.
about_author: Sable Crane is the pen name of a former aviation-industry analyst who spent a decade inside compliance departments before walking away with nothing but notebooks. They write thrillers about people who know exactly how systems fail because they once signed off on the failures.

chapters.title: Four Names, One Inbox
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. We meet them mid-disguise in Rotterdam, taking an unattributable case from a lawyer who pays in cash: records of Flight 4471 are vanishing mid-flight. The emotional beat is wary competence — Oscar trusts systems, not people, and the case already smells like a trap.

chapters.title: The Plane That Wasn't There
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Cross-checking radar archives, Oscar confirms the aircraft is still transmitting transponder pings while every booking, crew roster, and flight plan has been scrubbed. Beat: cold dread hardening into obsession.

chapters.title: Ilse Answers at 3 A.M.
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. A Frankfurt controller notices the ghost signal and calls the number hidden in a maintenance log. Her voice cracks when she admits her brother Tobias is listed on a manifest she can no longer see. Beat: two strangers recognizing each other's fear.

chapters.title: What the Wipe Cost
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Following payment trails, Oscar finds the deletion was bought three times over — by three different governments — meaning three motives stacked on one plane. Beat: vertigo; the case is bigger than any client.

chapters.title: Vess Takes the Contract
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. The assassin reviews her file on 'the archivist' and notes, with professional irritation, that her target has four names and no face. Beat: predatory calm, first hint she reads contracts more carefully than her employers do.

chapters.title: Dead Drop in the Rain
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A source in Brussels hands over a fragment of the original manifest before dying in an 'accident' twelve hours later. Beat: guilt — Oscar's tradecraft got someone killed, and duty starts to feel like complicity.

chapters.title: Tobias, Seat 14C
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse reconstructs her brother's day from receipts and memory, humanizing the erased passengers. Beat: grief as resistance; remembering becomes an act of defiance.

chapters.title: Three Governments, One Lie
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar maps why each government needed the flight gone: a defector, a weapons deal, a minister aboard. Any one truth burns all three. Beat: grim clarity — there is no safe version of this story.

chapters.title: The Man Who Knew My Second Name
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. A stranger greets Oscar by a name they buried years ago; it's Vess, introducing herself as a friendly colleague. Beat: terror laced with fascination — the hunter is charming, and that's worse.

chapters.title: Safehouse Arithmetic
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse shelters Oscar in Frankfurt, breaking every rule she's ever followed. Over bad coffee they trade their histories. Beat: tenderness under time pressure; love arriving at the least convenient hour.

chapters.title: Protocol vs. Person
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The lawyer offers Oscar extraction and a new fifth name if they drop the case. Beat: the book's thematic hinge — Oscar realizes every name they've worn was an escape, not a life.

chapters.title: Vess Reads the Fine Print
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess discovers her contract obliges her to erase witnesses *after* the markets open — meaning her employers planned to erase her too. Beat: the assassin becomes a variable, not yet an ally.

chapters.title: Night Over the Control Tower
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Ilse smuggles Oscar into the tower to pull raw radar data; alarms, near-misses, a supervisor bought off. Beat: adrenaline and trust — Ilse stakes her career and her brother's memory on Oscar's hands.

chapters.title: The Manifest Fragment
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Assembled from three sources, the full passenger list reveals a fourth party: a private intelligence firm that orchestrated the wipe and sold it thrice. Beat: revelation as betrayal — even the buyers were marks.

chapters.title: Contact
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Vess corners Oscar, gun drawn, and instead asks what the manifest says about her own handler. Beat: uneasy truce; two professionals negotiating with honesty as currency.

chapters.title: Everything Burns Except the Truth
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. The firm torches Oscar's safehouses and identities; all four names become liabilities overnight. Beat: loss and liberation — with nothing left to hide behind, only the truth remains.

chapters.title: Frankfurt, Before Open
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. Dawn. The team has until market open to broadcast the manifest; Ilse works the tower, Vess watches the exits, Oscar prepares the upload. Beat: taut stillness, love confessed in logistics.

chapters.title: The Assassin's Choice
chapters.summary: Vess's POV. Her handler orders her to kill both of them. She kills him instead, citing the contract's own fine print. Beat: catharsis — duty inverted into conscience.

chapters.title: Markets Open
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. At 9:00:04, the manifest hits every terminal in Frankfurt; the firm's stock collapses and governments scramble to claim credit for transparency. Beat: triumph with a bitter aftertaste — truth wins, but slowly.

chapters.title: Flight 4471 Lands
chapters.summary: Ilse's POV. The plane, rerouted and low on fuel, lands safely; Tobias walks into the arrivals hall. Beat: release — Ilse's vigil ends in an embrace, and Oscar watches from the crowd, unnamed and weeping.

chapters.title: Three Names Left
chapters.summary: Oscar's POV. Oscar testifies under one name, surrendering it to the record, and keeps the others like old coats. Vess vanishes owing them nothing. Beat: quiet reckoning — identity as something chosen, not hidden.

chapters.title: A Debt Repaid
chapters.summary: Oscar and Ilse's alternating POV, closing scene. Months later, in a small flat above the Rhine, Oscar takes a call about another vanished flight — and looks at Ilse before answering. Beat: belonging; the whistle-blower finally has someone to come home to.
